newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices steady despite crude drop.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices steady despite crude drop.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished Friday steady from Thursday's levels despite a decline in crude prices amid reports that Iraq would suspend recent military maneuvers, industry sources said.
"(Cash) resid prices are stagnant...but swap values are coming off," said one East Coast trader.
New York harbor one percent sulphur swaps were quoted at $19.20-$19.40, down from Thursday's $19.30-$19.60 a barrel. In the Gulf, three percent paper was flat at $16.35-$16.65.
"The offers are steady, but the bids are coming down. The ranges have widened," a Houston trader said.
The domestic resid market rose sharply this week on a rally in crude tied to U.S.-Iraq tension and above-market priced physical transactions.

NYMEX October crude futures settled down 49 cents at $24.51 a barrel, off from the highest prices since the end of 1991 set Thursday. NYMEX October Henry Hub natgas futures ended up 5.1 cent at $1.864 per million British thermal units.

In the New York harbor, one percent sulfur resid grade was quoted at $18.75-$19.25 a barrel, unchanged from Thursday's range. NYH three-percent grade was pegged at $16.25-$16.75, also flat from Thursday's level.
In the Gulf, prices for the one-percent grade ended at $17.25-$18.75, lower than Thursday's range of $17.50-$18.00. Three-percent values were quoted at $16.75-$17.25, unchanged from Thursday's range.
